chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zayd ibn al-Hasan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was the most similar to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in food and manner, and he used to eat bread and oil, and he used to feed the people bread and meat.'

He said: 'And 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to fetch water and gather firewood, and Fatima (peace be upon her) used to grind, knead, bake, and stitch. She was of the most beautiful of people in face, as if her two cheeks were two roses. May Allah bless her, and her father, and her husband, and her purified children.'
ai.seo_question: What were the daily habits and characteristics of Imam Ali and Fatima according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* underscores the concept of *Shabah* (likeness) between Imam Ali and the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that spiritual proximity is manifested through asceticism (*zuhd*) and shared domestic labor rather than royal privilege. It illustrates the ideal of the Ahl al-Bayt as a model of humility, where the leader serves his family, thereby validating the status of Fatima al-Zahra as the 'Mother of her Father' through her active participation in household duties despite her noble lineage.
